problemSolved: Represents an end-user browser, mobile app, or external API consumer initiating an HTTPS request to a workload running inside the HCP Guest Cluster.
interactions: Sends HTTPS requests to the cluster's public Route hostname resolved by external DNS.
TLS is terminated at the Shared Ingress Proxy running in the Bare Metal Cluster.
explorationCommands:
# Simulate a request from outside the cluster
curl -v https://<route-hostname>/api/endpoint

problemSolved: A cluster-wide singleton Deployment running in the 'hypershift' namespace of the management cluster — one instance manages every HostedCluster on the cluster, not one per guest. It reconciles HostedCluster and NodePool CRs, creates each guest's HCP namespace, and deploys the per-HCP control-plane-operator that in turn owns the individual control-plane components.
interactions: Watches HostedCluster and NodePool custom resources in the management API Server.
Creates the dedicated HCP namespace per hosted cluster and deploys the control-plane-operator into it.
Runs the NodePool controller, translating NodePools into Cluster API objects and delegating to the infrastructure provider (KubeVirt/CAPK, AWS, Azure, bare-metal Agent).
explorationCommands:
# Check HyperShift operator status
oc get pods -n hypershift

# List all HostedClusters
oc get hostedcluster -A

# View a HostedCluster spec
oc get hostedcluster <name> -n <namespace> -o yaml

problemSolved: The top-level HCP API object. A HostedCluster CR (in the management cluster's 'clusters' namespace) declares the desired guest control plane: release image, networking, platform (KubeVirt here), and publishing strategy. The HyperShift Operator reconciles it into a running control plane.
interactions: Authored by the platform admin and stored in the management API Server.
Reconciled by the HyperShift Operator, which derives the HCP namespace and a HostedControlPlane CR from it.
Surfaces overall control-plane availability and version in its status.
explorationCommands:
# List HostedClusters
oc get hostedcluster -A

# Inspect a HostedCluster's conditions
oc get hostedcluster <name> -n clusters -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions}'

problemSolved: The HCP abstraction for a set of identical worker nodes — the hosted-cluster analogue of a MachineSet. A NodePool CR declares replica count, instance type/VM template, and the release/upgrade strategy for the guest workers. There is no standalone Machine API in the guest; worker scaling is driven entirely through NodePools.
interactions: Authored by the platform admin alongside the HostedCluster, stored in the management API Server.
Reconciled by the HyperShift Operator's NodePool controller into Cluster API objects (Cluster, MachineDeployment).
Scaling or changing the NodePool replica count adds or removes guest worker VMIs.
explorationCommands:
# List NodePools for a hosted cluster
oc get nodepool -n clusters

# Scale a NodePool
oc scale nodepool <name> -n clusters --replicas=3

# Inspect NodePool status
oc get nodepool <name> -n clusters -o yaml

problemSolved: Manages the lifecycle and upgrade path of the guest OpenShift cluster. It applies the release payload, reconciles cluster operators, and enforces version constraints between components.
interactions: Reads the ClusterVersion CR to determine target version.
Applies manifests from the release image to the guest API Server.
Monitors ClusterOperator status and blocks upgrades when operators are degraded.
explorationCommands:
# View cluster version and upgrade status
oc get clusterversion

# Check cluster operator conditions
oc get clusteroperators

# View CVO logs
oc logs -n <hcp-namespace> deployment/cluster-version-operator --tail=50

problemSolved: The per-hosted-cluster operator (CPO) that the HyperShift Operator deploys into each HCP namespace. While the HyperShift Operator is a single cluster-wide controller, the CPO is the one that actually reconciles this guest's individual control-plane components — etcd, Guest API Server, OAuth, Konnectivity, Ignition, OVN control plane — into existence.
interactions: Reconciles the HostedControlPlane CR created by the HyperShift Operator.
Creates and manages the Deployments/StatefulSets for every guest control-plane component in the HCP namespace.
Wires up certificates, kubeconfigs, and service endpoints between the components.
explorationCommands:
# Check the control-plane-operator pod
oc get pods -n <hcp-namespace> -l app=control-plane-operator

# View CPO logs
oc logs -n <hcp-namespace> deployment/control-plane-operator --tail=50

# Inspect the HostedControlPlane it reconciles
oc get hostedcontrolplane -n <hcp-namespace> -o yaml

problemSolved: The upstream Cluster API (CAPI) controller manager running in the HCP namespace. It reconciles the Cluster, MachineDeployment, MachineSet, and Machine objects that the HyperShift NodePool controller generates, driving the generic machine lifecycle while delegating infrastructure to a platform provider.
interactions: Reconciles Cluster API Machine/MachineSet/MachineDeployment objects in the HCP namespace.
Delegates infrastructure creation to the platform provider (cluster-api-provider-kubevirt here).
Reports Machine status (provisioning, running, deleting) back up to the NodePool controller.
explorationCommands:
# Check the CAPI manager pod
oc get pods -n <hcp-namespace> -l control-plane=capi-controller-manager

# List the Machines for this hosted cluster
oc get machines.cluster.x-k8s.io -n <hcp-namespace>

# View MachineDeployment status
oc get machinedeployment -n <hcp-namespace>

problemSolved: The cluster-api-provider-kubevirt (CAPK) controller. It is the KubeVirt-specific Cluster API infrastructure provider: for each Machine, it creates a KubeVirt VirtualMachine object in the HCP namespace, which KubeVirt then realises as a running VirtualMachineInstance acting as a guest worker node.
interactions: Watches KubevirtMachine objects produced by the CAPI manager.
Creates and manages KubeVirt VirtualMachine / VirtualMachineInstance objects in the HCP namespace.
Reports VM readiness and node addresses back to Cluster API.
explorationCommands:
# Check the CAPK provider pod
oc get pods -n <hcp-namespace> -l control-plane=capi-kubevirt-controller-manager

# List the VirtualMachines backing the worker nodes
oc get vm -n <hcp-namespace>

# Inspect a KubevirtMachine
oc get kubevirtmachine -n <hcp-namespace> -o yaml

problemSolved: The Kubernetes API Server for the guest cluster, running as a Pod in the bare metal cluster. All kubectl/oc commands targeting the guest cluster reach this process. It handles authn/authz, admission webhooks, and persists state to the co-located etcd.
interactions: Exposes the guest cluster's API on a dedicated Service port.
Persists objects to the Etcd Static Pod instance in the same namespace.
Notifies guest controllers (scheduler, controller-manager) of state changes via watch events.
explorationCommands:
# Get guest API server URL
oc get hostedcluster <name> -n <ns> -o jsonpath='{.status.controlPlaneEndpoint}'

# Check guest API server health
curl -k https://<guest-api-endpoint>/healthz

# View API server logs
oc logs -n <hcp-namespace> deployment/kube-apiserver --tail=50

problemSolved: Handles OpenShift OAuth authentication flows for the guest cluster, issuing tokens to users. It runs as a Pod in the bare metal cluster, isolated from the guest node infrastructure.
interactions: Validates identity provider credentials and issues OAuth tokens.
Integrates with the Guest API Server for RBAC enforcement.
Stores sessions and tokens in the bare metal cluster etcd.
explorationCommands:
# View OAuth server logs
oc logs -n <hcp-namespace> deployment/oauth-server --tail=50

# Check OAuth routes on the guest cluster
oc get route oauth-openshift -n openshift-authentication

problemSolved: Runs the core Kubernetes control loops for the guest cluster as a single Pod in the bare metal cluster: NodeLifecycleController, EndpointController, DeploymentController, and others. Ensures desired state is reconciled continuously.
interactions: Watches the Guest API Server for resource events.
Manages ReplicaSet scaling, Endpoint slice population, and node health.
Writes status updates back to the Guest API Server.
explorationCommands:
# View controller manager logs
oc logs -n <hcp-namespace> deployment/kube-controller-manager --tail=50

# Check controller leases
oc get lease -n kube-system

problemSolved: Watches the Guest API Server for Pods with no assigned node and binds them to guest worker nodes based on resource availability, taints, tolerations, and affinity rules.
interactions: Watches Guest API Server for pending Pods.
Evaluates guest node capacity reported by guest kubelet via guest API Server.
Writes binding objects back to the Guest API Server to finalize scheduling.
explorationCommands:
# View scheduler logs
oc logs -n <hcp-namespace> deployment/kube-scheduler --tail=50

# Inspect scheduling events for a guest pod
oc describe pod <pod-name> -n <ns> | grep -A5 Events

problemSolved: The distributed key-value store that persists all guest cluster state. In HCP it runs as a StatefulSet Pod inside the guest's HCP namespace in the management cluster — not as a static pod (static pods only exist on kubelet-managed nodes via /etc/kubernetes/manifests). It stores every Kubernetes object (Pods, ConfigMaps, Secrets, CRDs) for the guest cluster.
interactions: Receives reads and writes exclusively from the Guest API Server.
Replicates data across the StatefulSet's etcd members via the Raft consensus protocol.
The control-plane-operator manages etcd member lifecycle and backups for this hosted cluster.
explorationCommands:
# Check etcd health
oc exec -n <hcp-namespace> etcd-0 -- etcdctl endpoint health

# List etcd members
oc exec -n <hcp-namespace> etcd-0 -- etcdctl member list

# Confirm etcd is a StatefulSet, not a static pod
oc get statefulset etcd -n <hcp-namespace>

problemSolved: An HAProxy-based ingress router running in the bare metal cluster that handles external HTTPS traffic destined for guest workloads. It terminates TLS for guest Routes and forwards traffic through the bare metal OVS fabric toward the target guest worker node.
interactions: Watches Route objects in the guest cluster via the Guest API Server.
Terminates TLS and proxies connections to guest Pod endpoints.
Traffic is forwarded via the bare metal cluster's OVS bridge to the KubeVirt Launcher.
explorationCommands:
# Check ingress proxy pods
oc get pods -n openshift-ingress

# View HAProxy config
oc exec -n openshift-ingress <router-pod> -- cat /var/lib/haproxy/conf/haproxy.config | head -60

# View Route objects
oc get route -A

problemSolved: The OVN-Kubernetes control plane Pod running in the bare metal cluster. It programs the OVN Northbound DB with logical network topology for the guest cluster, translating Kubernetes Network Policies and Services into OpenFlow rules.
interactions: Watches the Guest API Server for Pod, Service, and NetworkPolicy events.
Writes to the OVN Northbound Database to update logical switch topology.
Northbound DB is synced to the OVN Southbound DB and pushed to each node's OVN controller.
explorationCommands:
# View OVN master logs
oc logs -n openshift-ovn-kubernetes daemonset/ovnkube-master --tail=50

# Inspect logical switches
ovn-nbctl show

# Check OVN southbound flows
ovn-sbctl lflow-list | head -30

problemSolved: Bridges the guest cluster with the underlying cloud infrastructure. It manages cloud-specific resources such as load balancers, routes, and node addresses by calling cloud provider APIs on behalf of the guest cluster.
interactions: Watches Node objects in the guest cluster for ProviderID fields.
Calls cloud provider APIs to provision or update load balancers for LoadBalancer-type Services.
Reports cloud-specific node metadata back to the Guest API Server.
explorationCommands:
# Check CCM logs
oc logs -n <hcp-namespace> deployment/cloud-controller-manager --tail=50

# List cloud provider resources
oc get nodes -o wide

problemSolved: Provides a secure tunnel from the bare metal cluster control plane to the guest worker nodes. Enables the Guest API Server to reach kubelet on guest nodes (for exec, logs, port-forward) without requiring direct network connectivity.
interactions: Maintains persistent tunnels from the bare metal cluster to Konnectivity Agents on each guest worker node.
Proxies API Server → kubelet calls (exec, logs, port-forward) through the tunnel.
Used by the Guest API Server for all node-targeted traffic.
explorationCommands:
# Check konnectivity server
oc logs -n <hcp-namespace> deployment/konnectivity-server --tail=50

# Verify tunnel health
oc get pods -n <hcp-namespace> -l app=konnectivity-server

problemSolved: Serves Ignition configuration payloads to guest worker nodes during their initial boot sequence. Enables zero-touch provisioning: each new node fetches its complete OS, kubelet, and certificate configuration from this endpoint.
interactions: Provides a TLS-secured endpoint serving node-specific Ignition configs.
Injects kubelet bootstrap certificates and static Pod manifests.
Called once per node boot; after that, the node's kubelet manages its own certs.
explorationCommands:
# Check ignition server
oc get pods -n <hcp-namespace> -l app=ignition-server

# View ignition config for a node (requires admin certs)
curl -k https://<ignition-endpoint>/ignition

problemSolved: The guest cluster's openshift-monitoring stack. Like in any OpenShift cluster, it runs as workloads on the guest worker nodes (inside the VMs) — not in the management control-plane namespace. It scrapes metrics from guest components and user workloads for alerting and capacity planning.
interactions: Scrapes metrics endpoints on guest cluster Pods and nodes from within the guest cluster.
Stores time-series data in a Thanos-backed Prometheus instance running on guest nodes.
Exposes metrics via the guest cluster's OpenShift monitoring console.
explorationCommands:
# Check monitoring stack (from the guest cluster)
oc get pods -n openshift-monitoring --kubeconfig <guest-kubeconfig>

# Query Prometheus directly
oc exec -n openshift-monitoring prometheus-k8s-0 --kubeconfig <guest-kubeconfig> -- promtool query instant http://localhost:9090 'up'

problemSolved: The node agent running on the bare metal master node. It runs the management cluster's own control plane as Static Pods read from /etc/kubernetes/manifests, and also manages the regular guest control-plane Pods scheduled onto this node.
interactions: Watches /etc/kubernetes/manifests and runs the management control plane (kube-apiserver, etcd, scheduler, controller-manager) as Static Pods.
Polls the Management Kube API Server for regular Pods assigned to this node, including guest control-plane Deployments.
Calls CRI-O over the CRI gRPC interface to manage container lifecycle and reports node status back to the management API Server.
explorationCommands:
# Check kubelet status on the master
systemctl status kubelet

# See which static pods the kubelet is running
ls /etc/kubernetes/manifests

# Inspect the master node object
oc get node <baremetal-master> -o wide

problemSolved: The OCI-compliant container runtime on the bare metal master node. It creates and runs the containers for both the management cluster's control-plane Static Pods and the guest control-plane Pods scheduled onto this node.
interactions: Receives gRPC CRI calls from the master kubelet.
Pulls control-plane images and sets up each container's namespaces and cgroups.
Invokes the OVN-Kubernetes CNI plugin to wire each container into the master node's OVS bridge.
explorationCommands:
# List running containers on the master
crictl ps

# Inspect the kube-apiserver static pod container
crictl inspect $(crictl ps --name kube-apiserver -q)

# View CRI-O logs
journalctl -u crio --no-pager | tail -50

problemSolved: The host-side Open vSwitch service driving the OVN integration bridge (br-int) on the bare metal master node. Every control-plane Pod veth pair and the Geneve overlay uplink connect through this bridge.
interactions: Manages the br-int OVS bridge and its port configuration on the master node.
Receives OpenFlow rules from the local OVN controller.
Handles Geneve encapsulation for control-plane traffic to the other management cluster nodes.
explorationCommands:
# Show OVS bridge topology
ovs-vsctl show

# Dump OpenFlow rules on br-int
ovs-ofctl dump-flows br-int | head -30

# Check OVS service health
systemctl status openvswitch

problemSolved: The per-node OVN-Kubernetes DaemonSet Pod running on the bare metal master node. It syncs the OVN Southbound DB flows to the local OVS bridge and runs the CNI plugin that wires control-plane Pods into the cluster network.
interactions: Runs the OVN controller that translates Southbound DB entries into OpenFlow rules on the master's br-int.
Invokes the CNI plugin to create veth pairs and assign IPs when control-plane Pods start.
Maintains the Geneve tunnel endpoints connecting the master node to the rest of the overlay.
explorationCommands:
# View OVN node logs
oc logs -n openshift-ovn-kubernetes -l app=ovnkube-node --tail=50

# List OVS flows on this node
ovs-ofctl dump-flows br-int

# Check OVN southbound DB entries
ovn-sbctl show

problemSolved: The Kubernetes API Server of the management (bare metal) cluster itself, running as a Static Pod on the master node. This is the API the HyperShift Operator talks to: it stores HostedCluster/NodePool CRs and the guest control-plane Deployments. It is distinct from the per-guest Guest API Server that runs as a regular Pod inside each HCP namespace.
interactions: Started directly by the master kubelet from a manifest in /etc/kubernetes/manifests, before any scheduler exists.
Persists all management cluster state to the Management Etcd Static Pod on the same node.
Serves the HyperShift Operator, CVO, and every controller that reconciles guest control-plane workloads.
explorationCommands:
# Confirm the API server static pod is running on the master
oc get pods -n openshift-kube-apiserver -l apiserver=true -o wide

# Check API server health locally on the node
curl -k https://localhost:6443/healthz

# View the static pod manifest
cat /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver-pod.yaml | head -40

problemSolved: The etcd key-value store for the management (bare metal) cluster, running as a Static Pod on the master node. It persists all management cluster state, including the HostedCluster, NodePool, and guest control-plane object definitions. Each guest cluster keeps its own separate etcd that runs as a Pod inside its HCP namespace.
interactions: Receives reads and writes exclusively from the Management Kube API Server on the same node.
Replicates writes across the master nodes' etcd members via the Raft consensus protocol.
Backed up and health-checked by the management cluster's cluster-etcd-operator.
explorationCommands:
# Check management etcd health
oc exec -n openshift-etcd etcd-<master> -- etcdctl endpoint health

# List etcd members
oc exec -n openshift-etcd etcd-<master> -- etcdctl member list -w table

# View the static pod manifest
cat /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd-pod.yaml | head -40

problemSolved: The kube-controller-manager of the management (bare metal) cluster, running as a Static Pod on the master node. It runs the core control loops (Deployment, ReplicaSet, Node, Endpoint) that keep the management cluster — including the guest control-plane Deployments — reconciled to desired state.
interactions: Watches the Management Kube API Server for resource events.
Scales the guest control-plane Deployments (Guest API Server, OAuth, etc.) created by the HyperShift Operator.
Manages node lifecycle and writes status updates back to the management API Server.
explorationCommands:
# Check the controller-manager static pod
oc get pods -n openshift-kube-controller-manager -l kube-controller-manager=true

# View controller leases
oc get lease -n kube-system

# View the static pod manifest
cat /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-controller-manager-pod.yaml | head -40

problemSolved: The kube-scheduler of the management (bare metal) cluster, running as a Static Pod on the master node. It assigns pending management cluster Pods — including the guest control-plane Pods and the KubeVirt Launcher Pods — to bare metal nodes based on capacity and constraints.
interactions: Watches the Management Kube API Server for Pods with no node assignment.
Evaluates bare metal node capacity, taints, tolerations, and affinity rules.
Writes Binding objects back to the API Server to place guest control-plane and KubeVirt Pods onto nodes.
explorationCommands:
# Check the scheduler static pod
oc get pods -n openshift-kube-scheduler -l app=openshift-kube-scheduler

# Inspect scheduling decisions for a control-plane pod
oc describe pod <pod> -n <hcp-namespace> | grep -A5 Events

# View the static pod manifest
cat /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-scheduler-pod.yaml | head -40

problemSolved: The node agent running on the bare metal worker node. It manages the lifecycle of Pods scheduled to this node — including the KubeVirt Launcher Pod — by instructing CRI-O to create and monitor containers.
interactions: Polls the Bare Metal API Server for PodSpecs assigned to this node.
Calls CRI-O via the CRI gRPC interface to manage container lifecycle.
Reports node and Pod resource usage back to the Bare Metal API Server.
explorationCommands:
# Check kubelet status
systemctl status kubelet

# View kubelet logs
journalctl -u kubelet -f --no-pager | tail -50

# Check node conditions
oc describe node <baremetal-worker-node>

problemSolved: The OCI-compliant container runtime on the bare metal worker node. It creates and manages containers for host-side Pods, including the KubeVirt Launcher container that wraps the guest Virtual Machine.
interactions: Receives gRPC CRI calls from the host Kubelet.
Pulls container images from the registry and creates container namespaces.
Invokes the CNI plugin to connect containers to the OVS bridge.
explorationCommands:
# List running containers
crictl ps

# Inspect the KubeVirt launcher container
crictl inspect $(crictl ps --name launcher | awk 'NR>1{print $1}')

# View CRI-O logs
journalctl -u crio --no-pager | tail -50

problemSolved: The host-side Open vSwitch service that drives the OVN integration bridge (br-int) on the bare metal worker node. All Pod veth pairs, the VXLAN/Geneve uplink, and the KubeVirt tap interface connect through this bridge.
interactions: Manages the br-int OVS bridge and its port configuration.
Receives OpenFlow rules from the local OVN controller.
Handles Geneve encapsulation for inter-node overlay traffic.
Connects the KubeVirt VM's tap interface to the overlay network.
explorationCommands:
# Show OVS bridge topology
ovs-vsctl show

# Dump OpenFlow rules
ovs-ofctl dump-flows br-int | head -30

# Check OVS service health
systemctl status openvswitch

problemSolved: The per-node OVN-Kubernetes DaemonSet Pod that runs on the bare metal worker node. It syncs the OVN Southbound DB flows to the local OVS bridge and manages the host-side CNI plugin for Pod network provisioning.
interactions: Runs the OVN controller that translates Southbound DB entries to OpenFlow rules.
Invokes the CNI plugin to create veth pairs and assign IPs when Pods start.
Manages the Geneve tunnel endpoints for cross-node traffic.
explorationCommands:
# View OVN node logs
oc logs -n openshift-ovn-kubernetes -l app=ovnkube-node --tail=50

# List OVS flows on this node
ovs-ofctl dump-flows br-int

# Check OVN SB entries for this node
ovn-sbctl show

problemSolved: The KubeVirt node agent — a DaemonSet Pod on every bare metal node that can host VMs. It is the component that actually realises a VirtualMachineInstance: when the API holds a VMI scheduled to this node, virt-handler creates and supervises the virt-launcher Pod, then drives the VM's lifecycle (start, migrate, stop) to match desired state.
interactions: Watches the management API Server for VirtualMachineInstances assigned to this node.
Creates and manages the virt-launcher Pod that wraps each qemu-kvm process.
Reports VMI phase and node-level virtualization health back to the API Server.
explorationCommands:
# Find virt-handler on the worker nodes
oc get pods -n openshift-cnv -l kubevirt.io=virt-handler -o wide

# View virt-handler logs for this node
oc logs -n openshift-cnv <virt-handler-pod> --tail=50

# List the VMIs it is managing
oc get vmi -A -o wide

problemSolved: A privileged Pod that wraps a single VirtualMachineInstance. It manages the QEMU/KVM process life cycle, sets up the virtual NIC (tap0) bridged to the host OVS network, and monitors the VM's health on behalf of the KubeVirt Virt-Handler DaemonSet.
interactions: Spawns and supervises the qemu-kvm process for the Guest Worker Node VM.
Creates a tap interface (tap0) and connects it to the host OVS bridge via a macvtap or bridge port.
Exposes virtio device interfaces (virtio-net, virtio-blk) to the guest OS.
explorationCommands:
# Find the launcher pod
oc get pods -n <hcp-namespace> -l kubevirt.io=virt-launcher

# Inspect qemu process
oc exec -n <hcp-namespace> <launcher-pod> -- ps aux | grep qemu

# View virtual NIC config
oc exec -n <hcp-namespace> <launcher-pod> -- ip link show tap0

problemSolved: A full RHCOS Virtual Machine running inside the KubeVirt Launcher, acting as a guest cluster worker node. It runs a full Kubernetes node stack (kubelet, CRI-O, OVS) and hosts application workload Pods for the guest cluster.
interactions: Registers with the Guest API Server as a standard Kubernetes Node.
Runs guest kubelet, CRI-O, and OVN-Kubernetes node DaemonSet inside the VM.
Network traffic enters and exits through the tap0 virtual NIC managed by the KubeVirt Launcher.
explorationCommands:
# SSH into the guest worker node (via virtctl)
virtctl ssh core@<vmi-name> -n <hcp-namespace>

# Check node status from guest cluster perspective
oc get nodes --kubeconfig <guest-kubeconfig>

# View qemu-kvm process on host
oc exec -n <hcp-namespace> <launcher-pod> -- ps aux | grep qemu

problemSolved: The Kubernetes node agent running inside the Guest Worker Node VM. It watches the Guest API Server (via the Konnectivity tunnel) for Pods assigned to this node and instructs the guest CRI-O to create them.
interactions: Connects to the Guest API Server endpoint via the Konnectivity tunnel.
Calls guest CRI-O to manage container lifecycle for workload Pods.
Reports node resource usage and Pod status back to the Guest API Server.
explorationCommands:
# Check kubelet inside the VM
virtctl ssh core@<vmi> -- systemctl status kubelet

# View guest kubelet logs
virtctl ssh core@<vmi> -- journalctl -u kubelet --no-pager | tail -50

problemSolved: The OCI-compliant container runtime inside the Guest Worker Node VM. It creates and manages containers for workload Pods running in the guest cluster, setting up network namespaces and cgroup hierarchies for each container.
interactions: Receives gRPC CRI calls from the guest Kubelet.
Invokes the CNI plugin to connect containers to the guest OVS bridge.
Sets up cgroup v2 hierarchies for workload Pod resource isolation.
explorationCommands:
# List containers inside the guest VM
virtctl ssh core@<vmi> -- crictl ps

# Inspect a container
virtctl ssh core@<vmi> -- crictl inspect <container_id>

# View CRI-O logs in guest
virtctl ssh core@<vmi> -- journalctl -u crio --no-pager | tail -50

problemSolved: Open vSwitch running inside the Guest Worker Node VM, driving the guest-side OVN integration bridge (br-int). All workload Pod veth pairs inside the VM connect through this bridge, and the guest OVN-Kubernetes DaemonSet programs its flow rules.
interactions: Manages the in-VM br-int OVS bridge for guest Pod networking.
Receives OpenFlow rules from the guest OVN-Kubernetes node DaemonSet.
Traffic exits the VM through the virtio-net interface to the host tap0 device.
explorationCommands:
# Show guest OVS topology
virtctl ssh core@<vmi> -- ovs-vsctl show

# Dump guest OpenFlow rules
virtctl ssh core@<vmi> -- ovs-ofctl dump-flows br-int | head -30

problemSolved: The OVN-Kubernetes DaemonSet Pod running inside the Guest Worker Node VM. It syncs the guest OVN Southbound DB to the in-VM OVS bridge and handles CNI requests for workload Pod network provisioning.
interactions: Runs the OVN controller that programs guest OVS flows.
Invokes CNI to create veth pairs for workload Pods inside the VM.
Maintains Geneve tunnel configuration for cross-node (cross-VM) traffic.
explorationCommands:
# View OVN guest node logs
virtctl ssh core@<vmi> -- oc logs -n openshift-ovn-kubernetes ovnkube-node-<id>

# Check guest OVN southbound DB
virtctl ssh core@<vmi> -- ovn-sbctl show

problemSolved: The node-side counterpart to the Konnectivity Server in the bare metal cluster. It maintains a persistent outbound tunnel to the Konnectivity Server, enabling the Guest API Server to reach the guest kubelet for exec, logs, and port-forward operations.
interactions: Opens a persistent TLS connection to the Konnectivity Server in the bare metal cluster.
Proxies API Server → kubelet traffic through the established tunnel.
Required for 'oc exec', 'oc logs', and 'oc port-forward' to work on guest Pods.
explorationCommands:
# Check konnectivity agent inside VM
virtctl ssh core@<vmi> -- oc get pods -n kube-system -l app=konnectivity-agent

# Verify tunnel connectivity
virtctl ssh core@<vmi> -- curl -k https://<konnectivity-server>:8091/healthz

problemSolved: A per-node CoreDNS DaemonSet Pod inside the Guest Worker Node VM. It caches DNS responses locally to reduce round-trip latency and serves as the DNS resolver for all Pods running on this node.
interactions: Configured as the upstream DNS server for all containers via the kubelet's clusterDNS setting.
Forwards cluster-local queries (*.svc.cluster.local) to the Guest CoreDNS in the bare metal cluster.
Caches resolved records to reduce lookup latency for busy workloads.
explorationCommands:
# Check node-level CoreDNS
virtctl ssh core@<vmi> -- oc get pods -n openshift-dns -l dns.operator.openshift.io/daemonset-dns=default

# Test DNS from a workload pod
oc exec <pod> -n <ns> -- nslookup kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local

problemSolved: An HAProxy-based OpenShift Ingress Router running as a Pod inside the Guest Worker Node VM. It watches Route objects in the guest cluster and proxies the decrypted HTTPS traffic — after TLS re-encryption by the Shared Ingress Proxy — to the correct workload Pod.
interactions: Watches Route objects in the guest cluster via the Guest API Server.
Receives traffic forwarded by the Shared Ingress Proxy through the host OVS fabric.
Forwards the request to the target Service's endpoint (frontend-workload-pod).
explorationCommands:
# Check guest ingress router
virtctl ssh core@<vmi> -- oc get pods -n openshift-ingress

# View guest routes
virtctl ssh core@<vmi> -- oc get route -A

# Inspect HAProxy config
virtctl ssh core@<vmi> -- oc exec -n openshift-ingress <router-pod> -- cat /var/lib/haproxy/conf/haproxy.config | head -40

problemSolved: The user-facing application container. Receives HTTP requests forwarded by the Guest Ingress Router, processes business logic, and returns responses. This is the terminal destination of the external traffic flow.
interactions: Listens on a private Pod IP address within the guest cluster network.
Receives traffic from the Guest Ingress Router via the in-VM OVS bridge.
May call the Back-End Workload Pod via east-west Service traffic within the guest cluster.
explorationCommands:
# Check workload pods
oc get pods -n e-commerce-prod -l app=frontend

# View app logs
oc logs -n e-commerce-prod deploy/frontend --tail=50

# Exec into the container
oc exec -it deploy/frontend -n e-commerce-prod -- /bin/sh

# Check listening ports
oc exec deploy/frontend -n e-commerce-prod -- ss -tlnp

problemSolved: The backend service container handling data processing, database access, and API logic for the guest application. Called by the Front-End Workload via internal Service routing within the guest cluster.
interactions: Exposes a ClusterIP Service consumed by the Front-End Workload.
Connects to persistent storage and external databases.
Communicates over the in-VM guest OVS bridge via the OVN virtual fabric.
explorationCommands:
# Check backend pods
oc get pods -n e-commerce-prod -l app=backend

# View backend logs
oc logs -n e-commerce-prod deploy/backend --tail=50

# Check service endpoints
oc get endpoints backend-svc -n e-commerce-prod

problemSolved: Provides network virtualization and isolation inside the Guest RHCOS VM. It gives each workload Pod a private routing table, IP address, and packet filtering space.
interactions: Attaches to a guest-side veth pair managed by the OVN-Kubernetes Guest Node DaemonSet.
Provisioned and configured by the guest CRI-O runtime via CNI instructions.
explorationCommands:
# Find the target host PID of the container
virtctl ssh core@<vmi> -- crictl inspect <container_id> | grep pid

# Enter the isolated network namespace
virtctl ssh core@<vmi> -- nsenter -t <PID> -n ip addr show

problemSolved: Enforces CPU, memory, and I/O resource limits for each container inside the Guest VM. Prevents a single runaway container from starving other workloads on the guest node.
interactions: Hierarchy created by guest CRI-O/runc when the container starts inside the VM.
Guest kubelet monitors cgroup usage and reports resource consumption.
OOM killer is triggered when a container exceeds its memory limit.
explorationCommands:
# Find cgroup path for a container
virtctl ssh core@<vmi> -- crictl inspect <container_id> | grep cgroupsPath

# View memory limit
virtctl ssh core@<vmi> -- cat /sys/fs/cgroup/<cgroup_path>/memory.max

# View CPU quota
virtctl ssh core@<vmi> -- cat /sys/fs/cgroup/<cgroup_path>/cpu.max

problemSolved: The actual application process running as PID 1 inside the container's PID namespace within the Guest VM. It is the leaf node of the entire HCP ownership chain.
interactions: Runs inside the intersection of a Network Namespace, cgroup slice, and PID namespace — all inside the Guest VM.
Receives inbound socket connections on its private Pod IP address.
Writes logs to stdout/stderr captured by the guest container runtime.
explorationCommands:
# Exec into the container
oc exec -it <pod-name> -n <namespace> -- /bin/sh

# View the process tree
oc exec <pod-name> -n <namespace> -- ps aux

# Check listening ports
oc exec <pod-name> -n <namespace> -- ss -tlnp
